title: Audience Reaction Simulator
outcome: Test creative variants against modeled audience segments before publishing
breakthrough: Creative direction gains an experimental feedback loop
lane: Creative production, media, brand, and experience design

phases.name: Phase 1 - Build the Audience Reaction Simulator Core

subphases.name: 1.1 Audience Reaction Simulator Domain Model and State Plane
work: Define typed world models, scenarios, actors, variables, and simulation runs required to test creative variants against modeled audience segments before publishing, with explicit versions and validation at every boundary.

Implement an owned persistent state layer optimized for visual identity, assets, campaigns, characters, music, spatial design, and audience response; include snapshots or event history when state changes over time.
Expose create, query, update, subscribe, and delete operations through local APIs plus an SDK that never requires private cross-runtime imports.

subphases.name: 1.2 Audience Reaction Simulator Execution Runtime
work: Build resumable workers and state machines that perform the core operation: test creative variants against modeled audience segments before publishing.
Add cancellation, idempotency, bounded retries, timeouts, quotas, sandbox limits, and deterministic recovery from partial failure.
Create a local simulator that can replay success, malformed inputs, disconnection, overload, provider loss, and restart recovery.

phases.name: Phase 2 - Make Audience Reaction Simulator Adaptive and Usable

subphases.name: 2.1 Audience Reaction Simulator Decision and Learning Engine
work: Implement scoring, planning, prediction, search, or optimization using generative media, multimodal embeddings, style control, procedural composition, and reaction simulation.
Create feedback signals from task outcomes and user corrections; update tunable behavior without silently changing hard safety limits.
Return confidence, alternatives, bottlenecks, and a concise machine-readable explanation for every important automated choice.

subphases.name: 2.2 Audience Reaction Simulator Interaction Surface
work: Build the primary experience in the creative studio, asset graph, style mixer, and spatial preview room, including live state, controls, errors, and recovery actions.
Add a CLI and typed client library so humans, agents, games, and third-party applications can operate the capability directly.
Stream progress and intermediate artifacts in real time so long operations remain inspectable, interruptible, and steerable.

phases.name: Phase 3 - Scale Audience Reaction Simulator into a Breakthrough Product

subphases.name: 3.1 Audience Reaction Simulator Offline, Edge, and Cloud Mesh
work: Implement local-only, hybrid, and cloud execution with explicit capability discovery and graceful behavior when optional peers disappear.
Add conflict-safe synchronization, workload placement, caching, backpressure, and failover across devices or nodes where the feature benefits from distribution.
Benchmark latency, throughput, memory, energy, network transfer, and cost; make the scheduler choose the best execution mode from measured constraints.

subphases.name: 3.2 Audience Reaction Simulator Signature Breakthrough
work: Implement the differentiating behavior: Creative direction gains an experimental feedback loop. Ship it as an opt-in executable mode, not a mockup.
Run adversarial, load, privacy, misuse, degraded-network, and recovery tests against the novel behavior; block unsafe automatic actions.
Package the feature as an independently installable capability with a live demo, sample integration, metrics endpoint, and rollback-safe release artifact.
